title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
Problem V of E443 treats a uniform elastic lamina (beam) of length AB = a that is clamped at both ends. Euler wants its free vibrations.

He uses the same mode shape as throughout the paper:
y(x) = A cos(ζx/a) + B sin(ζx/a) + C e^{ζx/a} + D e^{-ζx/a}.
This is the general solution of the Euler–Bernoulli equation y'''' = (ζ/a)^4 y, after separating out the time factor cos(θθt).

At both ends y = 0 and y' = 0. This gives four homogeneous equations:
- I. A + C + D = 0 (y = 0 at x = 0)
- II. B + C − D = 0 (y' = 0 at x = 0)
- III. A cos ζ + B sin ζ + C e^ζ + D e^{-ζ} = 0 (y = 0 at x = a)
- IV. −A sin ζ + B cos ζ + C e^ζ − D e^{-ζ} = 0 (y' = 0 at x = a)

Euler eliminates A and B separately:
- III·cos ζ − IV·sin ζ gives A = C e^ζ(sin ζ − cos ζ) − D e^{-ζ}(sin ζ + cos ζ). With A = −C − D from I, C/D = [e^{-ζ}(sin ζ + cos ζ) − 1]/[e^ζ(sin ζ − cos ζ) + 1].
- III·sin ζ + IV·cos ζ gives B = −C e^ζ(cos ζ + sin ζ) − D e^{-ζ}(sin ζ − cos ζ). With B = −C + D from II, C/D = [e^{-ζ}(sin ζ − cos ζ) + 1]/[1 − e^ζ(cos ζ + sin ζ)].

On the next page the two expressions for C/D are equated (cross-multiplied). This yields the frequency equation 2 = cos ζ (e^ζ + e^{-ζ}), i.e. cos ζ cosh ζ = 1. That is the same equation as for the free–free beam of Problem I.

The page opens by completing the previous corollary. The pinned–clamped and pinned–free laminae share the frequency equation tan ζ = tanh ζ. Euler phrases this as a proportion: free end : pinned end :: pinned end : clamped end. The next page turns this into the remark that the clamped–clamped and free–free beams give the same tones.
errors: None. Both eliminations and both expressions for C/D check out algebraically. Cross-multiplying them does give cos ζ cosh ζ = 1.

A minor unremarked subtlety: the equivalence with the free–free case holds only for the nonzero roots. The free–free beam also has rigid-body modes at ζ = 0, which the clamped–clamped beam lacks. Euler's tables list only nonzero roots, so the comparison is correct as stated.

ideas.what: Clamped–clamped boundary conditions set up as a 4×4 homogeneous system; the frequency equation is obtained by eliminating constants
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E443, 1772/73); also Daniel Bernoulli for earlier beam vibration cases
ideas.where_published: E443, Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 17 (1772/73); discussed in Truesdell's Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11)

ideas.what: Frequency equation cos ζ cosh ζ = 1, identical for clamped–clamped and free–free beams
ideas.modern_name: Isospectrality of clamped–clamped and free–free beams (apart from the zero modes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; the free–free equation goes back to Euler and D. Bernoulli in the 1740s
ideas.where_published: E443; the free–free case also appears in the Additamentum to the Methodus inveniendi (E65, 1744)

ideas.what: Proportion: free : pinned :: pinned : clamped (pinned–free and pinned–clamped share tan ζ = tanh ζ)
ideas.modern_name: Boundary-condition duality for the fourth-order beam operator (y ↔ y'' exchanges the condition pairs)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Observation is Euler's (E443); the duality explanation appears in later vibration and inverse-problem literature (e.g. Gladwell)
ideas.where_published: E443, corollaries to Problems IV and V

missed.claim: Euler records the coincidences of spectra and calls them an 'insignis affinitas', but gives no structural reason. The reason is the map y → y''. If y is a clamped–clamped mode, w = y'' satisfies w'' = k⁴y = 0 and w''' = k⁴y' = 0 at the ends, so w is a free–free mode. Euler had all the ingredients but did not state this.
missed.quote: ex quo sequitur terminum liberum perinde se habere ad terminum stylo defixum, vti terminus stylo defixus, se habet ad terminum muro infixum
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This duality is known in modern beam and inverse-spectral theory. It is therefore not new, only an unexploited hint in the original; it has little novelty value.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds a correct, routine derivation of the well-known clamped–clamped frequency equation. The clamped/free equivalence is an established result attributed to this very paper and discussed by Truesdell.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is accurate. The final denominator is printed as '−e^ζ(cos ζ + sin ζ) + 1', which matches the derivation.
